Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 65, verse 1:

Explanation of the words:

"O Prophet": God addresses the Prophet ﷺ with this call, and his community is included, as shown by what follows.

"When you divorce women": that is, when you intend to divorce them.

"Divorce them for their waiting period": that is, at the beginning of their waiting period (qubul 'iddatihinna), namely in a state of purity (tuhr) in which he has not had intercourse with her.

"And count the waiting period": that is, keep track of its duration so that you can take her back (ruju') during it.

"And fear your Lord": that is, obey Him in His commands and prohibitions.

"Do not expel them from their houses": that is, do not drive the divorced woman out of the house of the husband who divorced her until her waiting period has ended.

"Unless they commit a clear immorality": that is, unless they harm others with obscene speech and bad conduct, or they commit a manifest indecency, which is clear adultery without any doubt.

"These are the limits of God": that is, the aforementioned rules: divorcing at the beginning of the purity period, counting the waiting period, and not expelling the divorced woman from her house until her waiting period has ended.

"You do not know; perhaps God will bring about after that some matter": that is, He will place in the husband's heart the desire to take her back, so he takes her back if she has not yet received the third divorce.

Meaning of the verse

His saying, exalted is He: "O Prophet, when you divorce women" — God, blessed and exalted, addresses the men of the Muslim community through the person of their Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, saying: "When you divorce," that is, when you intend to divorce them for a reason that requires it, "then divorce them for their waiting period," that is, at the beginning of their waiting period, which is in a state of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her, so that this purity counts as the first part of her waiting period.

His saying, exalted is He: "And count the waiting period" — that is, keep it, and know its beginning and its end, because of the rulings that depend on it: whether taking her back is valid or not, and maintenance and housing, or their absence.

His saying: "And fear God, your Lord" — so carry out His commands, and stop at His limits, and do not transgress them. "Do not expel them" — that is, the divorced women — "from their houses in which they were divorced, nor should they leave," that is, it is obligatory that they not leave their houses, "unless they commit a clear immorality," such as manifest adultery, or she is bad-mannered and foul-tongued, harming the people of the house with harm they cannot bear; in that case her expulsion is then permitted.

His saying, exalted is He: "These are the limits of God" — that is, the aforementioned rules of divorcing at the beginning of the purity period, counting the waiting period, and not expelling them from their houses. His saying: "Whoever transgresses the limits of God" — who goes beyond them and does not stop at them — "has wronged himself and exposed himself to the punishment of God, sooner or later."

His saying, exalted is He: "You do not know; perhaps God will bring about after that some matter" — that is, God may place in the man's heart a desire to take back his divorced wife, so he takes her back, and in that there is much good.

Guidance from the verse:

From the guidance of the verse:

1. Explanation of the Sunnah regarding divorce, which is that he divorces her in a state of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her.

2. That the divorce be a single pronouncement, not two or three.

3. The obligation of counting the waiting period, so that the husband knows when his divorced wife's waiting period ends, because of the rulings that depend on it regarding return (ruj'ah), maintenance and housing.

4. The prohibition of expelling a divorced woman from the house in which she was divorced until her waiting period has ended, except if she commits a manifest immorality such as adultery, or foul speech, or bad conduct and ugly treatment; in that case her expulsion is permitted.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 65, Verses 2–3**

**Explanation of the words:**

﴿فَإذا بَلَغْنَ أجَلَهُنَّ﴾: i.e., they approach the end of their ʿiddah (the waiting period).

﴿فَأمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾: i.e., take them back in a good manner, without harm.

﴿أوْ فارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾: i.e., leave them until their ʿiddah ends, and do not harm them by taking them back.

﴿وأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ﴾: i.e., call two just witnesses from among you to witness the divorce and the return (raj'ah), that is, from among the Muslims, so that no disbeliever bears witness.

﴿وأَقِيمُوا الشَّهادَةَ لِلَّهِ﴾: i.e., do not bear witness for the one against whom it is given, nor for his benefit, but for God Almighty alone.

﴿ذَلِكُمْ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ﴾: i.e., that which is mentioned from the beginning of the surah of rulings is what is enjoined, and it is carried out by whoever believes in God and the Last Day.

﴿ومَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ﴾: i.e., in His commands and prohibitions, so that he does not disobey Him in either.

﴿يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجاً﴾: i.e., a way out from the distress of this world and the Hereafter.

﴿ويَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ﴾: i.e., from where he does not expect or hope.

﴿فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ﴾: i.e., He is sufficient for him in what concerns him of his religion and his worldly affairs.

﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْراً﴾: i.e., regarding divorce, the ʿiddah, and other matters, He has set a limit, a term, and a measure at which each thing ends.

**Meaning of the two verses:**

The noble context continues to explain the ʿiddahs and the rulings of divorce and return (raj'ah). God says: ﴿فَإذا بَلَغْنَ﴾, meaning the divorced women, ﴿أجَلَهُنَّ﴾, i.e., they approach the end of the ʿiddah. ﴿فَأمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾, i.e., take them back on the basis of good companionship and noble fellowship, not to harm them, such as when a man takes her back and then divorces her again so that the ʿiddah is prolonged for her. This is not permissible, because harming people is forbidden. In a hadith: "There shall be no harm and no reciprocating harm." As for His saying ﴿أوْ فارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾, it means that he gives her what remains of her mahr (bridal gift) and provides her with mutʿah (a gift of provision) according to his circumstances, whether wealthy or poor.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿وأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ﴾, i.e., call witnesses to the marriage, the divorce, and the return. As for calling witnesses to the marriage, it is a pillar, and the marriage is not valid without it. As for divorce and return, it is recommended, and divorce and return may be valid without it. It is required that the witnesses be just, and that they be Muslims, not disbelievers.

His saying: ﴿وأَقِيمُوا الشَّهادَةَ لِلَّهِ﴾, i.e., perform it in its proper manner, and do not regard in it anything but the Face of God, Mighty and Majestic.

His saying: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَنْ كانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ﴾, i.e., that which you are commanded from the beginning of the surah, such as divorcing during a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her, counting the ʿiddah precisely, not expelling the divorced woman from her house, retaining her in good manner or releasing her in good manner, calling witnesses to the marriage, divorce, and return, and upholding justice in testimony. All of this is enjoined, i.e., ordered, and carried out by the believer in God and the Last Day, for he is the one who fears God's punishment and chastisement, so he does not venture into disobeying Him.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿ومَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجاً ويَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ﴾. This verse was revealed concerning ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī, who came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, my son has been captured by the enemy, and his mother is distressed. What do you order me?" He said: "I order you and her to frequently say: There is no power and no might except with God."

The woman said: "Excellent is what he has ordered you." So they both kept reciting it frequently. The enemy became heedless of their son, so he drove off their sheep and brought them to his parents, and this verse was revealed. It is general for everyone who fears God, Exalted, for He will make for him a way out from every constriction and a relief from every distress, and provide for him from where he does not hope or expect, and it does not occur to his mind. Whoever relies upon God, Exalted, in his affairs and does not neglect God's command or waste His rights, God, Exalted, will suffice him in what concerns him of his religion and his worldly life.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ أمْرِهِ﴾, i.e., He carries out His command among His servants, and they can never overpower Him. ﴿وقَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْراً﴾, i.e., a measure, a time, and a place, so it neither advances nor delays, nor increases nor decreases. Whoever is content, for him is contentment, and whoever is angry, for him is anger, and nothing occurs in God's dominion except what God wills.

**Guidance from the two verses:**

1. A return (raj'ah) is valid only during the ʿiddah. If the ʿiddah ends, there is no return for the divorced woman, and she may marry whomever she wishes, he or another, from the moment her ʿiddah ends.

2. Returning in order to harm is not lawful; it is lawful only for kindness, benevolence, and good companionship.

3. The legitimacy of calling witnesses to both the divorce and the return.

4. Justice is required in the witnesses. If justice is scarce among people, more witnesses are called.

5. God's true promise of a near relief for everyone who fears Him, Glorified and Exalted, and provision from where one does not hope.

6. Affirmation of the creed of divine decree and predestination (qadaʾ wa qadar).

7. God's sufficiency for whoever relies upon Him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 65, verses 4–5:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa-allaʾī yaʾisna min al-maḥīḍ* (وَاللَّائِي يَئِسْنَ مِنَ الْمَحِيضِ): and the women who have despaired of menstruation, i.e., the women who have given up on menstruating.

*In ir-tabtum* (إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ): i.e., if you doubt regarding their waiting period.

*Wa-allaʾī lam yaḥidna* (وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ): i.e., due to old age or young age.

*Wa-ulāt al-aḥmāl* (وَأُولَاتُ الْأَحْمَالِ): i.e., those who are pregnant, the women who are with child.

*Ajalahunna* (أَجَلُهُنَّ): i.e., at the completion of their waiting period, that they give birth to their burden.

*Dhālika amr Allāh* (ذَلِكَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ): i.e., that which has been mentioned regarding the waiting period and its details.

*Anzalahu ilaykum* (أَنزَلَهُ إِلَيْكُمْ): i.e., so that you may act upon it and implement its requirements.

The meaning of the two verses:

The noble context continues to explain the rulings on divorce, return (ruj'ah), and the waiting period (ʿiddah). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation﴾, i.e., due to their old age, such as a woman who has passed fifty years of age, when she is divorced after consummation. ﴿If you are in doubt, O believers, regarding their waiting period﴾, then their waiting period is three months. ﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾, i.e., due to their youth likewise, their waiting period is three months. And His saying ﴿and for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth to their burden﴾, i.e., the pregnant women, if they are divorced or their husbands die, their term at the completion of their waiting period is that they deliver their burden. Whenever she gives birth to the fetus in her womb, her waiting period has ended, even if she delivered it before completing nine months, provided she did not deliberately abort it by the abortion known today among the disbelievers.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾, i.e., among you, O believers, in these rulings concerning divorce, return, and the waiting period, so that he does not oppose His command in them, Allah will reward him from His bounty, making for him from His command ease (yusr), so that his affair is made easy for him, He provides him with what gladdens his eye, and sets his affairs in order.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is the command of Allah which He has sent down to you﴾, i.e., that which has been mentioned of the rulings in this surah concerning divorce, return, and the waiting period and their details, is the ruling of Allah which He has sent down to you so that you may comply and act upon it. So act upon it and do not neglect it, out of obedience to Allah and fear of His punishment. And whoever fears Allah in His commands and prohibitions, performing the obligations and avoiding the prohibited things, He will remove his misdeeds and magnify his reward for him, i.e., forgive him his sins and admit him into Paradise.

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1. Clarification of the waiting periods, which are as follows:
 1. A woman whose husband has died and who is not pregnant: her waiting period is four months and ten nights.
 2. A woman whose husband has died and who is pregnant: her waiting period is the delivery of her child.
 3. A divorced woman who does not menstruate due to old age or young age, and who has been consummated with: her waiting period is three months.
 4. A divorced woman who menstruates: her waiting period is three *qurū'* (قُرُوء), meaning she begins with the menstrual period that follows the purity in which she was divorced; or three periods of purity, likewise—it is all permissible. The word *qurʾ* (قَرْء) is shared, indicating both menstruation and purity.

2. It shows that the rulings on divorce, return, and the waiting periods are among what Allah revealed and sent down in His Book, so it is obligatory to act upon them, and it is never permissible to change or alter them by personal reasoning (ijtihad).

3. The virtue of piety (taqwa), and that it is the gateway to all ease and good in this world and the Hereafter.

2. It shows that the rulings on divorce, return, and the waiting periods are among what Allah revealed and sent down in His Book, so it is obligatory to act upon them, and it is never permissible to change or alter them by personal reasoning (ijtihad).

3. The virtue of piety (taqwa), and that it is the gateway to all ease and good in this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 65, verses 6–7:

Explanation of the words:

"Min wujdikum" (according to your means): i.e., according to your capacity, such that a man lodges his divorced wife in part of his dwelling.

"Wa la tudarruhunna" (and do not harm them): i.e., do not seek to harm them in any way whatsoever, whether in housing or in maintenance.

"Litudayyiqu 'alayhinna" (in order to constrict them): i.e., so that you constrict their housing, whereupon they leave it to you and go out from it.

"Wa in kunna ulati hamlin" (and if they are pregnant): i.e., pregnant, carrying fetuses in their wombs.

"Fa in arda'na lakum" (then if they nurse for you): i.e., your children.

"Fa-atuhunna ujurahunna" (then give them their wages): i.e., give them their wages for nursing; this is concerning divorced women.

"Wa'tamiru baynakum bima'ruf" (and consult among yourselves in kindness): i.e., and consult one another, or let each of you advise the other with a matter that concludes with agreement on a reasonable wage, neither excessive nor deficient.

"Wa in ta'asartum" (and if you disagree): i.e., if the mother refuses to nurse, or the father refuses to pay the wage.

"Liyunfiq dhu sa'ah" (let the wealthy spend): i.e., let the one of wealth spend on the divorced nursing women from his wealth.

"Wa man qudira 'alayhi rizquh" (and whoever has his provision restricted): i.e., whoever has his livelihood constricted, let him spend according to his condition.

Meaning of the two verses:

After clarifying divorce in its two types, the revocable and the irrevocable, and clarifying the waiting period according to its variations, the Exalted explained in these two verses the rulings on maintenance and nursing, saying: ﴿Lodge them where you dwell, according to your means﴾, i.e., according to your capacity, and do not harm them with any harm, neither in housing, nor in maintenance, nor in anything else, in order to constrict them so that they leave the housing for you and go out. These are the women divorced with a revocable divorce, whether pregnant or not. And His saying ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they deliver their burden﴾, i.e., and if the divorced woman is one with a final divorce, that is, he divorced her three times, then spend on them until they deliver their burden, i.e., house them and spend on them until they give birth. If she delivers her child, then both have the choice: if she wishes, she nurses his child for a wage they agree upon; and if he wishes, he may have the child nursed by a nurse other than its mother. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿If they nurse for you, then give them their wages, and consult among yourselves in kindness﴾, and that is accomplished through exchanging opinions until agreement on a specified wage. And if they disagree, such that each one makes the other's position difficult, i.e., they haggle over the wage and do not agree, then let him have another woman from among the women of the town nurse for him (the husband).

And His saying: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him﴾: The Exalted commanded the believer, when he divorces, to spend on his divorced woman who nurses his child for him, or who is in her waiting period in his house, according to his ease and hardship, or his wealth and poverty, since Allah does not burden a soul except with what He has given it of ability, wealth and means. The judge is the one who assesses the maintenance when there is dispute, and it is according to the man's income and the property he possesses.

And His saying: ﴿Allah will bring about ease after hardship﴾: This is a true promise which He fulfilled for the companions of His Messenger, when they were in hardship, and then the kingdoms of Chosroes and the Romans were opened to them, and their hardship was replaced with ease. As for others, it is conditional upon piety, as has preceded: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair.﴾

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The obligation of housing and maintenance for a woman divorced with a revocable divorce.

2- The obligation of housing and maintenance for a divorced pregnant woman until she delivers her burden.

3- The obligation of housing and maintenance for a woman whose husband has died while she is pregnant.

4- For the irrevocably divorced woman and the one divorced with a final divorce, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not rule for them either housing or maintenance, based on the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, sister of al-Dahhak. Among the grace that should not be forgotten: if she is in need of housing or maintenance, her former husband should house her and spend on her for the duration of her waiting period. His reward is great, because he has done good, and Allah loves the good-doers.

5- The obligatory maintenance is according to the condition of the divorcing man, whether wealthy or poor, and the judge assesses it if they dispute.

6- The woman divorced with an irrevocable divorce, if she nurses her child, has a wage for her nursing according to the agreement of both parties, the mother and the father.

7- Clarification of the general rule, which is that no soul is burdened except according to its capacity.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 65, verses 8–12:

Explanation of the words:

﴿وكَأِيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ﴾ (wa-ka'ayyin min qaryah): i.e., and many a town (qaryah, a city).

﴿عتت عن أمر ربها﴾ ('ataat 'an amr rabbiha): i.e., they disobeyed, meaning its people disobeyed their Lord and His messengers.

﴿عذاباً نكراً﴾ ('adhaaban nukran): i.e., terrible.

﴿ذكراً رسولاً﴾ (dhikran rasulan): i.e., the Qur'an, and He sent to you a messenger, who is Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿من الظلمات إلى النور﴾ (min al-zulumat ila al-nur): i.e., from the darknesses of disbelief and polytheism to the light of faith and monotheism.

﴿قد أحسن الله له رزقاً﴾ (qad ahsana Allahu lahu rizqan): i.e., the provision of Paradise, whose bliss never ends, ever.

﴿ومن الأرض مثلهن﴾ (wa-min al-ard mithlahunn): i.e., seven earths, one earth above another, just as the heavens are heaven above heaven.

﴿يتنزل الأمر بينهن﴾ (yatanazzalu al-amr baynahunn): i.e., the revelation between the heavens and the earth.

﴿لتعلموا أن الله على كل شيء قدير﴾ (li-ta'lamu anna Allaha 'ala kulli shay'in qadir): i.e., I inform you of that great creation and the wondrous descent so that you may know...

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted had established the rulings on divorce, reconciliation, the waiting period, and maintenance, and said that this was a command of God which He sent down to you and made obligatory to act upon, He warned in this verse against neglecting these rulings, ignoring them, and failing to uphold them. He said: ﴿And how many a town﴾, i.e., many cities whose people became arrogant (ʿataw), i.e., rose up haughtily against the commands of God and His messengers, so they did not comply with them, and against the rights, so they did not fulfil them. God reckoned with it in this world with a severe reckoning and punished it with a terrible punishment, i.e., dreadful. So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair, i.e., its punishment, and the outcome of its affair was loss, i.e., ruin and destruction. And God has prepared for them a severe punishment, which is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. In the repetition of the warning there is a caution against falling into it through polytheism and wrongdoing.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So fear God﴾, i.e., fear His punishment, so do not neglect His rulings or render them void, lest there befall you what befell others who were arrogant towards the command of their Lord and His messengers. O people of understanding, i.e., the intellects, who have believed: He has indeed sent down to you a reminder, which is the Qur'an, ﴿a messenger﴾, who is Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿reciting to you the clear verses of God﴾, clear in themselves, with no concealment or obscurity in them, so that He may bring out those who believed and did righteous deeds from the darknesses, i.e., the darknesses of disbelief and polytheism, into the light, the light of faith, monotheism, and righteous action.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; God has indeed made good provision for him﴾: this is a generous promise from a merciful Lord, promising everyone who believes in Him and does righteous deeds that He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and that He has made good provision for him therein, which is the bliss of Paradise that never runs out and never ends, forever.

As for His saying: ﴿God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them﴾, i.e., seven earths, one above another, just as the heavens are heaven above heaven. This is God, the one truly worthy of worship, besides whom there is no god and other than whom there is no lord.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That you may know that God is over all things competent, and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾, i.e., I inform you of His great creation of the heavens and the earths, and of the descent of the command between them at every time and moment, so that you may know that He, the Exalted, is competent over all things, so that you may desire what is with Him, and that He has encompassed all things in knowledge, so that you may fear Him and be mindful of Him; and by that you prepare yourselves for His favour and His pleasure.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A warning against abandoning the legal rulings, neglecting them, and toying with them.

2- An explanation of God's favour upon this nation in sending down the Qur'an to it and sending a messenger to it.

3- An explanation that disbelief is darkness and that faith is light.

4- An explanation of the greatness of God, the Exalted, and the breadth of His knowledge.
